## Which tours through La Paz should you choose?

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. They all include [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), but the city's role varies. On some itineraries, La Paz is the starting point for exploring Bolivia. On others, travelers spend time walking through its historic center and visiting the surrounding area. Multi-country journeys through Peru or Chile may devote only part of the trip to the city.

**The main question is how much time you want in La Paz and what matters most afterward: Lake Titicaca, Uyuni or continuing to a neighboring country.** If you are primarily interested in the city's history, look for a program with a dedicated sightseeing day. If natural scenery is the main attraction, La Paz can be the start of a wider journey across the Andes.

Our [Bolivia guide](/bolivia/) introduces the country's geography; this page is specifically for comparing tours that pass through La Paz.

## Comparing itineraries: the city, Titicaca, Uyuni and neighboring countries

| Itinerary | Best suited to |
|---|---|
| [La Paz, Tiwanaku and Uyuni](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-moon-valley-la-paz-tiwanaku/) | Andean culture and the salt flats in 7 days |
| [Bolivia in 11 days](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) | Titicaca, La Paz, lagoons and Torotoro |
| [Treasures of Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) | A broader journey across the country |
| [Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) | A connected route through two countries |
| [Bolivia and Chile in 16 days](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) | The Altiplano, Atacama and Patagonia |

On the [seven-day Bolivia itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-moon-valley-la-paz-tiwanaku/), the urban portion covers La Paz, [Moon Valley](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/) and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). The journey then continues to [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/), [Isla del Sol](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/) and the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). It is a good option for combining city experiences and natural landscapes in a relatively short time.

The [11-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) covers more ground, including [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), southwestern lagoons and [Torotoro](/bolivia/place/torotoro/). In La Paz itself, travelers enjoy a city tour and a trip to Moon Valley. This is a full itinerary with considerably more transfers. If you prefer a relaxed pace, compare the time spent on the road with the time available for walks.

[Treasures of Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) is worth considering for its multiple regions. Look not only at the stop in La Paz but also at how time is divided among cities, high-altitude areas and natural attractions.

On the [Peru and Bolivia tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), La Paz is part of a route connecting 2 countries. On the [Bolivia and Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/), it is combined with Uyuni, Altiplano lakes, the Atacama and southern Chile. When comparing such trips, check how much time is actually spent in Bolivia: the total number of days does not tell you how many will be spent in La Paz.

## What to see in La Paz itself

La Paz occupies a deep mountain basin. Buildings climb its slopes, so even a short trip between neighborhoods reveals changing views of the city and nearby peaks. Plaza Murillo, the historic streets and the [Witches' Market](/bolivia/place/la-paz-witches-market/) are worthwhile city sights, with the market linked to local crafts and ritual traditions.

A distinctive form of local transport is the Mi Teleférico cable-car network. Its lines reveal the structure of La Paz: lower neighborhoods, densely built slopes and neighboring El Alto. However, **the presence of cable cars in the city does not mean that a ride is included in every tour**. Look for it specifically in your chosen program's schedule.

Another possible stop is [Moon Valley](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/) in the Mallasa area, with a landscape of rock formations carved by erosion. If you want to explore the city, its natural surroundings and the [Tiwanaku archaeological complex](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) in depth, allow separate time for each rather than treating them as a single short city tour.

Individual city visits can be arranged from the [Bolivia excursion selection](/bolivia/excursion/). The [Bolivia culture and history tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/) are another way to find itineraries where history and local traditions form a substantial part of the trip.

## Why La Paz and Lake Titicaca make a practical combination

[Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/) and [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) often follow La Paz on the same itinerary. Travelers cross the Altiplano and may then visit [Isla del Sol](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/). The sequence makes sense: city life and history first, followed by the high-altitude lake, small settlements and ancient sites.

There is also a logistical consideration. The drive takes a substantial portion of the day, while island visits depend on boat schedules and weather. Distinguish between tours that devote a full day to Titicaca and those that place the lake between two long transfers.

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is a different matter: it is much farther from La Paz, and itineraries may include a flight or a long overland journey. Some tour packages include the flight, while others list it separately. Compare each offer's "Included" and "Not included" sections rather than inferring inclusions from the route map.

## Altitude, weather and the best order of stops

La Paz sits at approximately 3,600 m above sea level, with different districts at different elevations. This is a high-altitude starting point for travelers arriving from lowland areas. A less strenuous first day is sensible, and individual altitude-related risks should be discussed with a doctor before traveling, particularly for people with heart or lung conditions. Traveling quickly onward to even higher lakes places additional demands on the body.

The Bolivian Altiplano generally has a drier period from roughly May to October and a rainy season from November to March. These are planning guidelines, not weather guarantees: conditions in the city and on mountain roads can be quite different. Even sunny days can be cold, with temperatures falling toward evening.

When comparing programs, check which flights and long transfers occur during the first few days, where the overnights are scheduled and whether there is time to adjust to the altitude. For itineraries combining La Paz, Titicaca and Uyuni, these details are often more important than a difference of one attraction.

## What to check before choosing

Start by identifying your main goal. For city walks and cultural excursions, select an itinerary with clearly specified city visits. For nature and history together, choose a program including Titicaca or Tiwanaku. If salt flats and flamingos at high-altitude lagoons are more appealing, compare the time allotted to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the [Altiplano lagoons](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/).

Then confirm the practical details: where the tour begins and ends, how many nights are included, which domestic flights are paid for, where a guide is provided and which excursions are optional. For multi-country tours, the sequence of border crossings and distribution of time among regions also matter.

The most useful question to ask the organizer is: **which exact days are devoted to La Paz, and what will you have time to see on those days?** The answer is more useful than simply finding the city's name in a tour title.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through La Paz

### Does every tour through La Paz include a city tour?

No. This catalog brings together itineraries with La Paz on the main route, but their city sightseeing programs differ. Check the day-by-day schedule and the included excursions for the specific tour.

### Can I combine La Paz, Titicaca and the Uyuni Salt Flats?

Yes. The [seven-day Bolivia itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-moon-valley-la-paz-tiwanaku/) follows this sequence, as do longer programs. Consider the number of transfers and modes of transport when choosing.

### Is La Paz suitable as a first stop after an international flight?

La Paz is a convenient transport hub but sits at high altitude. The first few days should account for arrival, how you feel and any further ascent.

### How is a tour through La Paz different from a La Paz city excursion?

A city excursion focuses on La Paz itself or its immediate surroundings. A tour may take several days or weeks and continue to Lake Titicaca, Uyuni or other countries. For exploring the city alone, see [Bolivia excursions](/bolivia/excursion/).

### Do I have to fly from La Paz to Uyuni?

No. Different itineraries use different arrangements, including flights and overland transfers. The selected tour's program specifies the transport and whether it is included in the price.

## Laguna Blanca in Bolivia: pale water on the high plateau

**Laguna Blanca** is in Potosí Department in southwestern Bolivia, near the border with Chile and the foot of Licancabur Volcano. The lake lies at about **4,350 meters** above sea level, in the dry high-altitude terrain of the Altiplano. Nearby [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) is known for its more vivid greenish water.

The name means "White Lagoon." Its pale water is associated with minerals and suspended particles; depending on light and wind, the color can look milky, grayish or slightly blue. The lagoon does not look the same on every visit. Dry banks, distant volcanic slopes and open skies make the scenery particularly striking in clear weather.

Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde are **two separate lakes**, even though they are close together and often appear on the same excursion itinerary. They should not be confused in photographs either: an image showing the bright turquoise water of neighboring Laguna Verde is not a documentary photograph of Blanca.

## Why the water looks white

Laguna Blanca is a saline lake in a closed high-altitude basin. Dissolved substances and suspended minerals accumulate in its water, while evaporation affects its composition. The suspended minerals account for the characteristic light color.

Color also depends on the direction of sunlight, cloud cover and the state of the water's surface. Wind changes the reflection of the sky and creates ripples, making the milky effect more or less pronounced. **Do not visit solely in the expectation of guaranteed white water**: variation is natural here.

Several lagoons with different colors lie in the same region. [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is known for its reddish tones and flamingos. [Laguna Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/) forms part of another section of the chain of high-altitude lakes. Visiting several locations reveals the diversity of the mineral environment rather than repeating the same scenery.

## Where Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde are located

Both lagoons lie in the southwestern part of the Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve area. Laguna Blanca has a larger surface area than neighboring Verde and is separated from it by a relatively narrow strip of land.

The main mountain landmark is Licancabur Volcano on the Chilean border. Its cone is familiar from panoramas of Laguna Verde, but volcanic terrain also shapes the landscape around Blanca.

These high-altitude lakes exist in a harsh climate. Moisture and water levels vary, while mineral deposits and rocky sections appear along the shores. Visits focus on viewing the lake from permitted stopping points; walking across unstable ground or all around the shoreline is not a required part of the itinerary.

## Visiting on an overland tour

Laguna Blanca is generally included in an extended four-wheel-drive route through southwestern Bolivia. Depending on the direction of travel, the vehicle heads from [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) toward the Chilean border or the other way around. The route passes volcanic deserts, geothermal fields, mineral lakes and high-altitude plains.

On Ada Tours' [16-day Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/), Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde are included on the Altiplano transfer day toward San Pedro de Atacama. This is **part of a much larger route through Bolivia and Chile**, so it should not automatically be understood as a lengthy standalone excursion around the lake.

When planning, confirm the route, vehicle and time available at each stop. Dirt roads, wind, snow or heavy rainfall can change travel times. The lagoons' proximity does not guarantee that every viewpoint will be accessible in bad weather.

## Altitude and traveler wellbeing

At around 4,350 meters, the air is thinner than in lowland cities. Even a short walk beside the lake can feel demanding, particularly after a rapid arrival from lower elevations. Cold winds and intense sunlight add to the discomfort.

Warm layered clothing, a windproof jacket, headwear, sunglasses, ultraviolet sunscreen and drinking water are useful on such a trip. If you develop a headache, nausea, pronounced weakness or difficulty breathing, inform your guide and seek medical assistance. It is best to discuss acclimatization with a doctor before traveling.

Parts of the lagoon are highly mineralized and are not suitable for recreational swimming. Do not enter the water or walk on mineral crusts where safety and permission to pass have not been established.

## When to plan the journey

The season mainly affects road access and weather conditions. Rainy months can cause washouts on high-altitude roads; in drier weather, cold nights and dusty winds may complicate travel. The color of the water also depends on the conditions on the day of your visit.

Think of this lagoon as part of a journey through southwestern Bolivia. Laguna Blanca offers pale mineral scenery, [Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) provides contrasting green tones below Licancabur, and [Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) has reddish shallows and wetlands. Together, they demonstrate the diversity of the high-altitude Altiplano.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Blanca

### Where is Laguna Blanca?

In southwestern Bolivia, in Potosí Department, close to the Chilean border, Laguna Verde and Licancabur Volcano.

### Why does Laguna Blanca look white?

The pale color is associated with high mineral content and suspended particles in the water. Light and wind change its appearance.

### Are Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde the same lake?

No. They are neighboring high-altitude lakes separated by a narrow strip of land. They have different names and characteristic water colors.

### Can Laguna Blanca be visited from Uyuni?

Yes. Many overland itineraries in the high-altitude southwest of Bolivia travel through the chain of colored lagoons between Uyuni and the Chilean border area. Exact stops and durations depend on the program.

### Can you swim in Laguna Blanca?

No. This is a high-altitude mineral lake, and visitors come to observe the natural landscape from permitted sections of the shore.

## Tours visiting Laguna Blanca: which trip is right for you?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. [Laguna Blanca](/bolivia/place/laguna-blanca/) lies in the southwestern Bolivian Altiplano among high-altitude salt lakes and volcanic slopes. Travelers come for views of its pale water, the mountains and nearby [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/).

The lake's role in the itinerary matters. It is generally **a stop on an extended four-wheel-drive journey**, rather than a place to relax for several days. Search for trips covering the entire route between [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the southern plateau lakes and the Chilean border, rather than just the lagoon's name.

## Which current itinerary includes Laguna Blanca?

On the [16-day private tour through Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/), Laguna Blanca is included on the main route. The transfer from the Uyuni Salt Flats toward San Pedro de Atacama includes [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), the [Polques hot springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), Laguna Blanca and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/).

A significant feature of that day is that **the road journey across the Altiplano and the border takes approximately 8–9 hours**. The lagoons are therefore visited as part of a busy transfer day. The itinerary does not provide for lengthy independent walks around each lake.

The route then continues through Chile, from San Pedro de Atacama toward other regions. Travelers choose this format to combine Bolivian salt flats and lagoons with the Atacama and Patagonia. If you want to focus only on southwestern Bolivia, compare it with the [Bolivia tour catalog](/bolivia/tour/), but do not assume that every Uyuni jeep tour necessarily visits Laguna Blanca.

## Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde: why visit both?

The two lakes are close together but look different. At Laguna Blanca, the water and banks often appear light because of the mineral composition and deposits. [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) is known for greenish-turquoise tones and views of Licancabur Volcano. The colors depend on light, wind and water surface conditions, so the same intensity of color cannot be guaranteed on every trip.

It makes sense to include both in the same stretch of the road. This offers a comparison of neighboring landscapes without separate long trips to each lake. However, *the fact that an itinerary names both lagoons does not establish how long each stop will last*. Refer to the specific tour's schedule for the sequence.

For a broader view of the region's nature, see the [Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). Its landscapes include volcanic mountains, deserts, mineral lakes and habitats for Andean birds.

## How the journey is organized and what to consider

Local roads run high above sea level and far from major settlements. Four-wheel-drive vehicles are used on the route; travel time depends on road conditions and the border crossing. **Laguna Blanca is part of an actual route across Bolivia and Chile, not a standalone lakeside excursion with a guaranteed duration.**

Plan for several practical considerations. Warm clothing and sun protection are both useful: winds and ultraviolet radiation are strong on the exposed plateau. Altitude requires attention to how you feel. Entry documents and current border procedures should be checked for each traveler's nationality and actual route.

Even when an itinerary lists [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and Laguna Blanca, check the sequence and duration of stops in the day-by-day program. That will make it easier to judge whether the journey suits photographers, travelers who prefer leisurely walks or those looking for a long adventure itinerary.

## When this kind of route makes sense

If seeing Laguna Blanca is a priority, select a program that **explicitly names it among the required stops on the main itinerary**. Multi-country tours offer more experiences but take more time and involve additional transfers. Other current [Bolivia-only routes](/bolivia/tour/) may suit a trip focused on the country, but you should check separately whether they visit this particular lagoon.

The weather in the southern Altiplano varies throughout the year. Roads are generally more predictable in the drier months, while the rainy season may require adjustments on some sections. A photograph of the water taken in one season does not guarantee the same appearance on your dates. A confirmed route, actual road conditions and what is included matter more when choosing.

Compare similar nature-focused trips in the [Bolivia wildlife and nature selection](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/), or browse the [multi-country tour catalog](/multi-country/) for journeys continuing into neighboring countries.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Laguna Blanca included on the 16-day Bolivia and Chile tour?

Yes. It is listed on the main itinerary of the [Bolivia and Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) during the transfer from Uyuni to San Pedro de Atacama.

### Will there be a full day devoted only to Laguna Blanca?

This itinerary does not set aside a separate day exclusively for the lagoon. The stop is included in a long transfer through several natural sites. The time available for sightseeing should be confirmed against the specific itinerary.

### How is Laguna Blanca different from Laguna Verde?

Blanca is known for its pale water and mineral shores, while [Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) is associated with greenish tones and a view of Licancabur Volcano. They are geographically close and are often visited together.

### Is this a swimming stop?

Swimming is not part of the lagoon visit. If you are interested in thermal bathing, the [Polques hot springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) are a separate destination. Check their inclusion and conditions in the chosen program.

## Laguna Cañapa: flamingos and mountain scenery in Bolivia

[Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) is a high-altitude lake in Potosí Department, southwestern Bolivia. Pale salt deposits, dry ground and wide-open Andean scenery alternate along its shores. Under suitable conditions, flamingos feed in the shallows.

Cañapa is part of extended overland itineraries through the Altiplano lagoons. Travelers stop here to observe birds, the water's colors and the surrounding volcanic mountains. It is a distinct natural site, even though neighboring lagoons may look similar in photographs.

## Where the lagoon is located

Cañapa lies in the high-altitude Nor Lípez area, approximately **4,100 m above sea level**. Dry slopes and volcanic uplands surround the lake, whose shorelines change in appearance with the season, wind and amount of water.

There is none of the familiar infrastructure of a lakeside resort here. Visitors generally arrive by four-wheel-drive vehicle on a route connecting the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) with the highlands farther south.

## Why flamingos visit

Shallow high-altitude waters provide feeding conditions for birds. Several Andean flamingo species may be seen around Cañapa, including the Andean, Chilean and James's flamingos. The presence of each species and the number of birds depend on the season and the lake's actual conditions.

Flamingos often stand in groups in shallow water, filtering small organisms from it. The best way to watch them is from the shore, leaving the birds space. People approaching too closely can cause them to stop feeding or move away.

A telephoto lens is useful for photographing wildlife. Do not attempt to walk directly across salt flats toward a flock: the ground can be wet and unstable, while disturbing the birds harms their habitat.

## How Cañapa differs from neighboring lagoons

Jeep itineraries often include this lake together with [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) and [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/). These are distinct bodies of water with differences in color, mineral deposits along the shore, numbers of birds and surrounding terrain.

At Cañapa, the contrast between water and dry mountain slopes is particularly striking. At other lagoons, an unusual mineral-water smell or the shape of the banks may attract attention. A single photograph cannot tell you in advance how many flamingos will be visible at each stop.

Farther south lies the famous [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), with its reddish hues. It is not part of Cañapa, although both appear on routes through the region.

## When Cañapa features on Ada Tours itineraries

On the [three-day Uyuni Salt Flats jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), Laguna Cañapa is visited on day 2, when travelers see Honda, Hedionda and Cañapa in sequence. The route then passes through the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) toward the [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/) and [Ollagüe Volcano](/bolivia/place/ollague-volcano/).

On the [11-day Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/), the high-altitude lagoons form part of a longer journey linking La Paz, Titicaca, Uyuni and Torotoro.

For photographers and wildlife enthusiasts, compare the time allocated to the high-altitude section rather than just the total length of the journey. The more stops there are in a day, the more important the road logistics become.

## When is birdwatching best?

The lagoon's conditions change over the year. Roads may be easier to use in dry months, but nights and mornings can be cold. During the rainy season, both water levels and access road conditions change.

Even in a suitable month, birds are not guaranteed. An old photograph cannot predict the size of a flock or the exact distance between the road and the water.

## Preparing for a high-altitude stop

An elevation of over 4 km affects wellbeing and the ability to tolerate exertion. Allow for acclimatization, move at an unhurried pace and bring warm clothes. Strong sunshine, wind and cold weather make sunglasses, a hat and drinking water important.

It is sensible to make the stop with a guide who knows the roads and permitted observation spots. Avoid venturing onto salt crusts of unknown strength.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Cañapa

### Are there flamingos at Cañapa?

Yes. This is one of the high-altitude lakes visited by Andean flamingo species. Their number and distance from visitors vary with conditions.

### Can you swim in the lagoon?

The lagoon is a natural observation stop, not a developed beach. Swimming in its mineral-rich water is not part of the itineraries described.

### Are Cañapa and Laguna Colorada the same lagoon?

No. They are separate lakes in southwestern Bolivia, visited on different sections of high-altitude routes.

### How do you reach Cañapa?

Usually by four-wheel-drive vehicle on a route through Uyuni, the lagoons and the Siloli Desert. The exact order depends on where the journey starts.

## Laguna Cañapa: an optional stop for birdwatching

[Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) lies in southwestern Bolivia amid high-altitude salt lakes and dry volcanic slopes. A stop on its shore offers a chance to observe the changing color of the water and, in favorable conditions, flamingos. Its open landscape gives even a short visit a sense of what the Bolivian Altiplano looks like beyond the vast Uyuni Salt Flats.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Cañapa as **an optional stop**. This is a separate choice to arrange when planning the trip. If birds and lagoons are your main interests, compare [tours with a scheduled visit to Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/tour/), where it is already part of the main itinerary.

## Adding Cañapa to a Peru and Bolivia itinerary

The [18-day VIP tour Machu Picchu, the Amazon and Uyuni Salt Flats](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) covers coastal Lima, an Amazon cruise, Andean cities and the Uyuni Salt Flats. The itinerary offers an **optional day 16** among the high-altitude lagoons. Cañapa is listed together with [Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), [Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/) and [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/).

For travelers, this is a chance to see another natural region during a longer journey through Peru and Bolivia. However, long dirt-road stretches and high altitude require advance planning. The word "optional" means the visit should not be treated as a required or already paid-for part of the itinerary.

It is particularly important to coordinate the added excursion with the return to Uyuni and the onward flight. On the VIP program, an airport transfer and a flight via La Paz follow the excursion. Departure time, feasibility of the entire route and vehicle arrangements must be confirmed when preparing the individual schedule.

## When to choose Cañapa

The main reason to add the lagoon is the opportunity to observe birds on open high-altitude water. Cañapa lies above 4,100 m; cold mornings, wind and strong sunshine can be noticeable even under clear skies. Birds move freely, while water levels and colors vary. An encounter with flamingos at a specific hour cannot be guaranteed.

| Priority | What to arrange |
|---|---|
| Flamingos | Time for a stop on the shore |
| Photography | Lighting and extra time |
| Comfort | Altitude, transport and clothing |

For greater variety in natural landscapes, it makes sense to combine Cañapa with neighboring lakes. [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) and [Laguna Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/) lie in the same high-altitude region but offer different viewpoints and scenery. Visiting several lagoons requires more time in the vehicle than making one short stop.

## Preparing for the optional excursion

Around Cañapa, solar radiation is intense and temperatures can change abruptly. For stops, bring a warm layer, a windbreaker, hat, sunglasses, closed shoes and drinking water. There is no need to approach the birds closely: binoculars or a zoom camera allow observation from a distance.

Discuss the high-altitude route in light of your previous acclimatization. Planning requires particular care if the preceding days include rapid flights from lowland regions. If you feel unwell, reconsider physical exertion and onward transfers, and discuss medical concerns with a doctor before traveling.

## Frequently asked questions about Cañapa

### Is Cañapa included in the core 18-day VIP tour?

In this program's description, Cañapa appears on **an optional Altiplano day**. This additional section is arranged before travel.

### Can I be guaranteed to see flamingos?

No. Cañapa is known for opportunities to observe high-altitude birds, but their presence and their distance from the shore depend on natural conditions.

### What other places can be combined with Cañapa?

The optional day also lists [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), [Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/) and [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/). The final schedule depends on roads and the time required for the return trip.
